coverage.headline: Israeli Court Says Papaya Gaming Should Improve Its Debt Settlement Proposal to Repay $730 Million to Skillz
coverage.summary: On August 26, 2026, Tel Aviv District Court Judge Lushi-Abudi rejected Papaya's motion to convene creditors' meetings to vote on its proposed debt settlement, ruling that Papaya's repayment plan relying solely on operating profits was insufficient and must be strengthened with additional capital sources. The judge also suggested that Papaya's managers and shareholders who received dividends could be required to contribute their own capital.

coverage.headline: Israeli court says Papaya Gaming should improve its debt settlement plan
coverage.summary: Judge Lushi-Abudi of the Tel Aviv District Court rejected Papaya's motion to convene creditors' meetings to vote on its proposed debt settlement, ruling that the plan — which relies solely on operating profits — must be strengthened with additional funding or security beyond current cash flows. The court stated Papaya should improve its repayment proposal before it can proceed to a creditor vote.

coverage.headline: Papaya Gaming wins U.S. bankruptcy protection after $719 million ruling
coverage.summary: Judge Mary F. Walrath of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware granted Papaya Gaming a temporary injunction, staying collection and enforcement proceedings against the company's U.S. assets and rejecting Skillz's demands for a financial guarantee. The ruling preserves the status quo pending a formal Chapter 15 recognition hearing.

coverage.headline: Papaya Gaming Files Chapter 15 After $719M Verdict
coverage.summary: Detailed the mechanics of Papaya's Chapter 15 filing, including the supervised fund arrangement presented to the Israeli court (~$100 million in 2026 plus ongoing contributions), and quoted bankruptcy attorney Sunni P. Beville explaining Chapter 15 as a procedural tool for foreign restructuring recognition, not a determination of company survival.

coverage.headline: Catching Up With New Bankruptcy Case Action (Oriel Bachar and Papaya Gaming Ltd.)
coverage.summary: Law360's Bankruptcy Authority roundup flagged Oriel Bachar and Papaya Gaming Ltd. as a notable new case filing, tracking docket activity in the Chapter 15 proceeding in the District of Delaware.

coverage.headline: Why a popular gaming company filed Chapter 15 bankruptcy
coverage.summary: TheStreet reports on Papaya Gaming's dual-track legal strategy: a Chapter 15 filing in Delaware and an Israeli court-supervised fund expected to hold approximately $100 million in 2026 as a potential source for settling claims. The company admits in the filing it cannot pay the $719 million judgment.

coverage.headline: Solitaire Cash maker files bankruptcy after $719M verdict
coverage.summary: Reported Papaya Gaming's August 3 Chapter 15 filing in Delaware following the July 27 verdict by Judge Cote, noting that if the petition is approved, Skillz/Firy would be blocked from collecting on the judgment while Papaya's appeal proceeds, and that Papaya's operations including Solitaire Cash continue as usual.

coverage.headline: Papaya Gaming seeks U.S. recognition of Israeli insolvency proceeding to stay $729M New York judgment
coverage.summary: Papaya Gaming applied for U.S. recognition of an Israeli insolvency proceeding in an attempt to stay the $729 million final judgment entered in New York, which it intends to appeal. The filing involves multiple Papaya entities globally, including Papaya Gaming Ltd., Papaya Gaming Inc., and affiliated international subsidiaries.

coverage.headline: Papaya Gaming wins temporary stay after $719 million US judgment
coverage.summary: The Tel Aviv-Jaffa District Court granted Papaya Gaming a temporary stay of proceedings as the company sought a court-supervised payment arrangement following the $719 million U.S. judgment, with Judge Iris Lushi-Avudi issuing the order while the court considers Papaya's proposed arrangement. A federal jury had found in April that Papaya used undisclosed bots in its skill-based mobile games.

coverage.headline: Papaya Gaming Files Ch. 15 To Shield Against $719M Verdict
coverage.summary: Israeli mobile gaming company Papaya Gaming filed a Chapter 15 bankruptcy petition in Delaware after being hit with a $719 million judgment in a New York federal court over false advertising claims involving the use of bots in its gaming tournaments. The filing seeks to shield U.S. assets from collection while Papaya appeals the ruling.

coverage.headline: Papaya Files Chapter 15, Concedes It Can't Pay $719 Million Judgment
coverage.summary: Casino.org reports that Papaya Gaming's Chapter 15 filing explicitly acknowledges it cannot satisfy the judgment owed to rival Skillz (now Firy), and describes the company's parallel Israeli court proceedings under which it will place approximately $100 million into a supervised fund in 2026.

coverage.headline: Papaya Gaming Ltd. et al: Chapter 15 Petition (Israel)
coverage.summary: OffshoreAlert documented the Chapter 15 Petition for Recognition of a Foreign Main Proceeding in Israel filed by Oriel Bachar, as Foreign Representative of Papaya Gaming Ltd. and Papaya Gaming Inc., at the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware on August 2, 2026. The filing seeks U.S. recognition of the Israeli insolvency proceeding in order to stay the approximately $729 million New York judgment.

coverage.headline: When 'Skill-Based' Isn't: The Papaya Gaming Verdict and Its Implications for Mobile Gaming Operators
coverage.summary: Legal analysis from Troutman Pepper attorneys Stephen Piepgrass and Ayana Brown examines Judge Cote's July 27 ruling in Skillz Platform Inc. v. Papaya Gaming Ltd. (No. 1:24-cv-01646), which awarded $719 million in disgorgement plus $10.1 million in fees, and explores regulatory implications for mobile gaming operators who misrepresent skill-based competition.

coverage.headline: Skillz Locks Up $719 Million Payout from Gaming Rival Papaya
coverage.summary: Bloomberg Law reported that Papaya Gaming Ltd. must pay more than $700 million in profits and attorneys' fees to mobile gaming rival Skillz Platform Inc. following a Manhattan federal judge's order. The ruling set the stage for Papaya's cross-border insolvency strategy.

coverage.headline: Papaya Owes $719M, Atty Fees In Gaming False Ad Case
coverage.summary: A New York federal judge granted Firy Inc.'s request ordering Papaya Gaming Ltd. to disgorge $719 million and pay $10.1 million in attorney fees, on top of a $420 million jury verdict from April for alleged misrepresentations about its mobile games using bots. The disgorgement figure replaced, rather than supplemented, the original damages award.

coverage.headline: Federal Court Orders Papaya Gaming to Pay $719 Million to Skillz Platform Inc., a FIRY (NYSE: FIRY) Company, Disgorging Its Unjust Profits From False Advertising
coverage.summary: Firy Inc. (NYSE: FIRY), formerly Skillz Inc., announced that the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York entered judgment against Papaya Gaming of $719 million in disgorgement plus approximately $10 million in attorneys' fees, replacing the jury's earlier $420 million actual-damages award. The court found that between 2021 and 2024, approximately 70% of Papaya's advertised prize money was won by bots, not real players.

coverage.headline: Game Co. Calls Out Rival's $1.4B Damages Enhancement Bid
coverage.summary: Papaya Gaming asked the Manhattan federal judge to deny Skillz's request to enhance the $420 million jury verdict to $1.4 billion, arguing the amount was unprecedented and exceeded Papaya's total profits over the relevant period. The court ultimately ordered a $719 million disgorgement figure, triggering Papaya's Chapter 15 filing.

coverage.headline: Papaya Gaming Found Liable by New York Jury in Skillz Case
coverage.summary: A Manhattan federal court jury found Papaya Gaming liable for false advertising and ordered the company to pay $420 million in damages to rival Skillz Platform Inc., a verdict that was later enhanced by Judge Denise Cote to $719 million in disgorgement in late July 2026.
